resources.title: Housing — Burnaby
resources.body: Average 1-bedroom apartment in Burnaby city centre is approximately CAD 2,350/month per Numbeo (Jul 2026). BC landlords typically require first month's rent as security deposit (maximum allowed by law). Kijiji.ca and rentals.ca are the primary rental portals.

resources.title: Banking — Burnaby
resources.body: Major Canadian banks serve Burnaby. Newcomers need passport, immigration document (work/study permit or PR card), proof of BC address, and SIN if available. RBC and TD Bank offer newcomer banking packages. Burnaby is part of Metro Vancouver, with full access to all major bank branches.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Burnaby
resources.body: Burnaby is served by Burnaby Schools (School District 41), which offers French Immersion, International Baccalaureate (IB), and Mandarin Language Arts programs. The district also has an international student program and settlement workers in schools for newcomers.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Burnaby
resources.body: Newcomers on work or study permits must notify IRCC of address changes via the IRCC portal. Permanent residents update SIN address with Service Canada. BC residents must exchange a foreign driving licence within 90 days of establishing BC residency via ICBC.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Burnaby
resources.body: A Social Insurance Number (SIN) is Canada's tax identification number, issued by Service Canada. Required for work, tax filing, and government benefits. Apply at a Service Canada office or online.

resources.title: Transport — Burnaby
resources.body: Burnaby is served by TransLink (Metro Vancouver's transit authority), including SkyTrain (Millennium and Expo lines) and buses. Adult monthly pass (1-zone) is CAD 117.20 (as of July 1, 2026 fare increase). Foreign licence holders have 90 days to exchange to a BC licence via ICBC. BC MSP (Medical Services Plan) has a 3-month wait period for new arrivals from outside Canada.

resources.title: Housing — Gatineau
resources.body: Average 1-bedroom apartment in Gatineau city centre is approximately CAD 1,545/month per Numbeo (Jun 2026). Quebec landlords may require 1 month security deposit, though Quebec law limits deposits to first month's rent only. Kijiji.ca and rentals.ca are primary rental portals.

resources.title: Banking — Gatineau
resources.body: Major Canadian banks serve Gatineau (across the Ottawa River from Ottawa). Newcomers need passport, immigration document, proof of Quebec address, and SIN if available. RBC and TD Bank both offer bilingual (French/English) newcomer banking services in the region.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Gatineau
resources.body: Gatineau is served by the Commission scolaire des Draveurs and Commission scolaire au Coeur-des-Vallees for French-language public schools, and the Western Quebec School Board for English-language public education. French is the language of instruction. Newcomers with children may need to meet Quebec language law requirements for school enrollment.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Gatineau
resources.body: Newcomers on work or study permits must notify IRCC of address changes via the IRCC portal. Permanent residents update SIN address with Service Canada. Quebec drivers must exchange a foreign driving licence within 90 days of establishing Quebec residency via SAAQ.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Gatineau
resources.body: A Social Insurance Number (SIN) is Canada's tax identification number, issued by Service Canada. Quebec residents also file provincial taxes with Revenu Quebec. SIN required for work, federal and provincial tax filing, and government benefits.

resources.title: Transport — Gatineau
resources.body: Gatineau is served by the STO (Societe de transport de l'Outaouais). Numbeo reports an average monthly transit pass of CAD 113 for Gatineau. The STO also connects to Ottawa's OC Transpo network. Foreign licence holders must exchange to a Quebec licence within 90 days via SAAQ. Quebec's RAMQ (Regie de l'assurance maladie du Quebec) health insurance has a 3-month waiting period for new residents from outside Canada.

resources.title: Housing — Mississauga
resources.body: Average 1-bedroom apartment in Mississauga city centre is approximately CAD 2,396/month per Numbeo (Aug 2026). Ontario landlords typically require first and last month's rent as deposit. Kijiji.ca and rentals.ca are primary rental portals.

resources.title: Banking — Mississauga
resources.body: Major Canadian banks serve Mississauga. Newcomers need passport, immigration document, proof of Ontario address, and SIN if available. RBC and TD Bank both offer newcomer packages. Numbeo reports an average monthly transit pass of CAD 141 in Mississauga.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Mississauga
resources.body: Mississauga is served by Peel District School Board (public) and Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board. International Baccalaureate (IB) and French Immersion programs are available. Peel DSB has a dedicated newcomer welcome centre program.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Mississauga
resources.body: Newcomers on work or study permits must notify IRCC of address changes via the IRCC portal. Permanent residents update SIN address with Service Canada. Ontario drivers must exchange a foreign licence within 60 days of becoming an Ontario resident.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Mississauga
resources.body: A Social Insurance Number (SIN) is Canada's tax identification number, issued by Service Canada. Required for work, tax filing, and government benefits. Apply at a Service Canada office or online.

resources.title: Transport — Mississauga
resources.body: MiWay (Mississauga Transit) operates the city bus network; PRESTO card is used. Adult monthly PRESTO pass is CAD 145. Newcomers must exchange foreign driving licences within 60 days in Ontario (via ServiceOntario/MTO). Ontario OHIP health card has no waiting period as of recent policy — coverage begins immediately upon eligibility determination.

resources.title: Housing — Regina
resources.body: Average 1-bedroom apartment in Regina city centre costs approximately CAD 1,481/month per Numbeo (Jun 2026). Saskatchewan landlords typically require first month's rent as deposit. Kijiji.ca is the main local rental portal.

resources.title: Banking — Regina
resources.body: Major Canadian banks serve Regina. To open an account as a newcomer, typical documents include passport, immigration document (work/study permit or PR card), proof of address, and SIN if available. RBC and Scotiabank both offer newcomer banking packages.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Regina
resources.body: Regina is served by Regina Public Schools and Regina Catholic School Division for K-12. International Baccalaureate (IB) programs are available at some secondary schools. The provincial curriculum is Saskatchewan-based.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Regina
resources.body: Newcomers on work or study permits must notify IRCC of address changes via the IRCC portal (ircc.canada.ca). Permanent residents register their SIN and may update address with Service Canada. Saskatchewan drivers must exchange a foreign licence within 90 days of establishing residency.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Regina
resources.body: A Social Insurance Number (SIN) is Canada's tax identification number, issued by Service Canada. Required for work, tax filing, and government benefits. Apply at a Service Canada office or online.

resources.title: Transport — Regina
resources.body: Regina Transit operates the city's bus network. Adult monthly pass is CAD 97. Numbeo reports average pass at CAD 88-97. Newcomers must exchange foreign driving licences within 90 days via SGI Saskatchewan. Saskatchewan health card (SK Health Card) has a 3-month wait period for new arrivals from outside Canada.

resources.title: Housing — Windsor
resources.body: Average 1-bedroom apartment in Windsor city centre is approximately CAD 1,660/month per Numbeo (Jun 2026). Ontario landlords typically require first and last month's rent as deposit. Kijiji.ca is the primary rental portal.

resources.title: Banking — Windsor
resources.body: Major Canadian banks serve Windsor. Newcomers need passport, immigration document, proof of Ontario address, and SIN if available. RBC and Scotiabank both offer newcomer banking packages. Windsor is close to the US border with access to cross-border banking services.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Windsor
resources.body: Windsor is served by the Greater Essex County District School Board (public) and Windsor-Essex Catholic District School Board. The GECDSB offers ESL, French as a Second Language, International Languages, and Special Education programs. International student programs are also available.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Windsor
resources.body: Newcomers on work or study permits must notify IRCC of address changes via the IRCC portal. Permanent residents update SIN address with Service Canada. Ontario drivers must exchange a foreign licence within 60 days of becoming an Ontario resident.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Windsor
resources.body: A Social Insurance Number (SIN) is Canada's tax identification number, issued by Service Canada. Required for work, tax filing, and government benefits. Apply at a Service Canada office or online.

resources.title: Transport — Windsor
resources.body: Transit Windsor operates the city bus network. Numbeo reports an average monthly transit pass of CAD 122.50 for Windsor. Transit Windsor is located at 300 Chatham Street West. Foreign drivers must exchange licence within 60 days in Ontario. Ontario OHIP health card coverage is available with no waiting period upon eligibility approval.
